children: Global manufacturers, utilities and miners have lost $4.2 trillion in market value since June as enthusiasm for AI infrastructure suppliers fades, the Financial Times reported. Its analysis found that companies most closely associated with data center construction suffered the steepest declines.

For investors, the retreat exposes the risks of valuing traditional industrial businesses on expectations of sustained AI growth. Concerns about debt-funded construction and political resistance are weighing on shares, even as suppliers report strong demand.
The losses erased nearly half the group’s $9.4 trillion gain over the preceding year. Caterpillar’s market value fell 44%, or $214 billion, from its June 30 peak. Nuclear developer Oklo
dropped 49%, while cooling specialist Comfort Systems
each lost roughly half their value.
Operating results offer a stronger picture. U.S. data center construction spending, excluding chips and IT equipment, reached $96 billion in the year through September. Caterpillar
reported a record $78 billion backlog and 75% annual growth in power-generation sales, while Eaton

Analysts disagree over how much protection those orders provide. Some expect backlogs to support revenue through 2027; others warn that customers reserving capacity with multiple suppliers could exaggerate underlying demand, according to the FT.

Construction restrictions backed by voters in recent U.S. elections add uncertainty. Citi researchers expect greater volatility but consider widespread building bans unlikely, while some economists anticipate projects shifting to more accommodating locations.

title: AI infrastructure sell-off erases $4.2T from industrial, energy stocks
